claim.pdf_says: READ statement, Format 2 (random): a single tall optional BRACKET encloses the whole KEY IS phrase, spanning BOTH rows of the inner brace - [ KEY IS { data-name-1 / record-key-name-1 } ] - with the bracket's lower arm printed below the 'record-key-name-1' row.
claim.why_it_matters: Everywhere else in this same figure a tall delimiter is transcribed by repeating it on each row ('{ NEXT }' / '{ PREVIOUS }', '[ WITH LOCK ]' / '[ WITH NO LOCK ]'). Here the outer bracket appears only on the first row, so under that convention the optional bracket looks as though it closes before 'record-key-name-1', leaving that alternative dangling outside any delimiter. No normative content is lost, but the notation is internally inconsistent and is easy to mis-transcribe on the next pass.

verdict.reasoning: Both sources were read directly. PDF (rendered at 300 dpi, cropped and magnified on the KEY IS group): the glyphs are a single tall square bracket whose upper arm sits above the 'KEY IS' row and whose lower arm sits below the 'record-key-name-1' row, enclosing 'KEY IS' followed by a tall brace containing 'data-name-1' over 'record-key-name-1'. So the claim's description of the PDF is accurate. Markdown (work unit line 46-47, identical to specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 29480-29481): '    [ KEY IS { data-name-1      } ]' / '             { record-key-name-1 }'. So the claim's quotation of the markdown is accurate too. The claim is nonetheless REFUTED as a content discrepancy: nothing the PDF prints is missing. Every syntactic element survives - the optionality bracket, the underlined reserved word KEY, the word IS, the choice brace repeated on BOTH rows, and both alternatives 'data-name-1' and 'record-key-name-1'. No choice indicator is lost; the braces are present on each row exactly as printed. The sole difference is the ASCII rendering STYLE of the outer tall bracket: drawn once on the first row rather than duplicated on the second. That is figure formatting, not content, and it changes no meaning - the derivable grammar is identical (the KEY IS phrase is optional; within it exactly one of the two names is chosen). The internal-inconsistency argument is also weaker than the claim asserts: this same figure already prints non-repeated material on the first row only - 'READ file-name-1 { NEXT     } RECORD [ INTO identifier-1 ]' / '                 { PREVIOUS }' - where 'READ file-name-1' and 'RECORD [ INTO identifier-1 ]' appear once and only the inner brace repeats. A reader of this file therefore already parses a second row as a continuation of the group begun on the first, and the KEY IS rows follow that established pattern ('KEY IS' likewise appears once). Reading the bare '{ record-key-name-1 }' row as a dangling alternative outside any delimiter is not a plausible parse - it would leave a choice brace with a single member and no enclosing phrase. The claim itself concedes 'No normative content is lost'. Per the reconciliation rules (reject when the difference is only formatting and does not change meaning), this is not a reportable discrepancy.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The PDF's tall optional bracket around the whole KEY IS phrase is rendered in ASCII with the bracket on the first row only ('[ KEY IS { data-name-1 } ]') while the continuation row carries just the repeated choice brace ('{ record-key-name-1 }'). All tokens, the choice braces and the optionality bracket are present and the meaning is unchanged. The only defensible nits are stylistic: (a) the outer bracket is not duplicated on the continuation row the way '[ WITH LOCK ]' / '[ WITH NO LOCK ]' duplicates its bracket, and (b) the closing braces are misaligned by one column ('{ data-name-1      }' is 20 characters against 21 for '{ record-key-name-1 }'). If ever normalized for tidiness the rows would read '[ KEY IS { data-name-1       } ]' / '[        { record-key-name-1 } ]', but the existing text is not wrong.
